findings.title: The entire flagged inverse axis is a scaled classical exact-descent-set count
findings.evidence: For every r>=0, m>=1 and A subset {2,...,m}, D_{r,m}(A)=binom(r+m,m)*beta_m(A-1). SOURCE_AND_PROOF.md section 4 proves this by completing w_j-1 to a length-r+m inversion code in r! ways and double-counting permutations with the prescribed suffix descent set. beta_m is exactly MacMahon's classical evaluated descent-set number. All 1785 isolated adapter cells and 16064 actual suffix-code prefix-multiplicity cells pass in the independent checker.
findings.impact: The target mask already comes from Theorem 2.2; after substituting the explicit owner adapter, no materially independent inverse mechanism remains in the fixed contract. The true temporal theorem alone does not meet this batch's two-axis admission bar.
findings.required_resolution: Reject the present two-axis paper admission and reopen its seat. No new author lemma or replacement contribution is supplied by this review.

observations.title: Phase masks distinguish source sets but not post-collapse fibre cardinalities
observations.evidence: Permutation complementation gives beta_m(S)=beta_m([m-1] minus S), hence D(r,m,A)=D(r,m,A-complement). All cardinalities at t>=2 coincide for a fixed target. Source 011 still has different targets 011 and 012 at times 2 and 3. The independent verifier uses 471132 pointwise phase-mask checks because aggregate count checks alone cannot test phase direction. The frozen m=2 offset example is correct and merely does not exclude a binomial scale times an unflagged exact-set count.
